extracted.intended_audience: scholars, journal editors, and practitioners interested in peer review and academic publishing
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and institutional functions for how scientific referees evaluate manuscripts; explains what refereeing does, what referees attend to, sources of disagreement, and normative expectations placed on reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality control / gatekeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Filter what enters the archive of certified knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refereeing functions as institutionalised quality control: referees decide which manuscripts become part of the formal scientific record by accepting or rejecting submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of recognition and esteem
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards of 'publication credit' calibrate symbolic rewards in science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions about publication affect career rewards and the distribution of prestige; reviewers therefore participate in assigning recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of journal space
rubrics_metrics.description: A scarce resource that referees ration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees help determine how limited pages/space in journals are distributed among competing contributions; considerations of novelty and importance often mediate this rationing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of error
rubrics_metrics.description: Detection of mistakes in evidence, reasoning, and presentation before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees are expected to spot factual, methodological, and logical errors and to prevent dissemination of flawed results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement of manuscripts (developmental function)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive criticism that raises the level of accepted work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond gatekeeping, referees often provide substantive feedback to help authors revise and strengthen argumentation, methods, and exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status-judgments on contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Cumulative evaluations that shape careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referee reports contribute to reputational standings and can have cumulative effects (e.g., the 'Matthew effect') influencing future opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinforcement of cognitive and methodological norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Refereeing socialises authors into the disciplinary standards of evidence, exposition and citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews transmit and enforce norms about acceptable methods, styles of argument, and citation practices within a field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / novelty of contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority claims and incremental advance: Is the contribution new?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees evaluate whether a paper makes an original or novel claim, differentiating genuine advances from mere replication or small incremental steps; attention paid to priority and originality verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of method
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of experimental design, statistical treatment, and theoretical derivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees judge whether methods are appropriate, correctly applied, and sufficiently rigorous to support the paper's claims; includes scrutiny of experimental controls, statistical analysis, and logical derivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequacy of data to support the paper's claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the presented empirical or theoretical evidence is sufficient, reliable, and properly interpreted to back the conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical coherence of argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal consistency and argumentative logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees check for clear, non-contradictory reasoning and whether conclusions follow from premises and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance / importance to the discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the paper 'advances the field'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the potential impact, relevance, or importance of the findings or arguments for ongoing scholarly conversations and the development of the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and economy of exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality, readability, and conciseness of writing and presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees consider whether the manuscript communicates ideas clearly and efficiently; poor exposition can be grounds for revision requests or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of citation to relevant literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Situating the work in the cognitive map of the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the author has acknowledged and engaged with pertinent prior work, provided correct attributions, and placed the contribution in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness for the specific journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Fit with the journal's audience and scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the manuscript matches the topical, methodological, and readership expectations of the target journal; suitability can be independent of intrinsic quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority and originality verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether claims duplicate or appropriately build on prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees check for overlooked prior publications and verify priority claims; failure to detect duplication may alter evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct in attribution of credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper attribution and avoidance of plagiarism or miscrediting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees are attentive to ethical issues around authorship, citation, and credit; improper attribution is a serious concern affecting acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank of the journal influences standards
rubrics_metrics.description: More prestigious journals demand stricter standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation thresholds vary by journal prestige; referees often apply higher novelty and significance expectations for top-tier outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank/status of the contributor affects judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: High-status authors may receive cumulative advantage ('Matthew effect').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees' perceptions of author credentials and institutional affiliation can bias evaluations, often favoring established names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of the referee conditions strictness
rubrics_metrics.description: Eminent referees tend to be more critical and less variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The social standing of reviewers correlates with their stringency and consistency; this stratification affects heterogeneity in decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differing cognitive standards across schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Disagreement arises from different disciplinary schools of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees from different theoretical or methodological traditions may apply divergent evaluative criteria, producing conflicting recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive theoretical disagreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflicting substantive interpretations of results or theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When referees disagree about core theoretical premises, their evaluations of the same manuscript may diverge substantially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential salience of method versus substance
rubrics_metrics.description: Some referees prioritize methodology, others emphasize substantive contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variation in what reviewers consider central (technique vs. result) explains part of inter-referee disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerance for speculative versus consolidative work
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences in acceptance of speculative/innovative vs. confirmatory work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees differ in appetite for risk: some penalize speculation while others value consolidation; this affects recommendations for novel or unconventional manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal/social biases (institution, school, nationality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-cognitive biases affecting referee judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referee decisions can be influenced by authors' institutional affiliations, school membership, nationality, or other social factors, producing potential unfairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinterestedness (normative expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judgments must not be coloured by personal interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees are expected to set aside personal gain or rivalries and evaluate on impersonal criteria; conflicts of interest should be declared or avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universalism (normative expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims judged by impersonal criteria, not by who advances them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should rest on merits of evidence and argument rather than author identity or status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communality (normative expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharing of knowledge required by referee-author exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees contribute to communal scientific knowledge by engaging with manuscripts and communicating findings and critiques to authors and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organised scepticism (normative expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every claim subject to critical scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees should apply critical appraisal systematically and rigorously to claims, methods, and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humility (normative expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that the referee may be wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be open to uncertainty and refrain from overconfident pronouncements; humility mitigates dogmatic rejection of novel work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality (normative expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve manuscript and review process confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees must not disclose or misuse privileged information contained in manuscripts or the review correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness (normative expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt response to review requests and timely reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although recognised as a chronic failure in practice, timely reviews are expected to keep the publication process efficient and fair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mertonian foundations for reviewer instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper articulates why referees evaluate (institutional functions), what they attend to (evaluative dimensions), and the normative obligations placed on them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conceptual elements form an implicit backbone for modern reviewer guidelines: combine procedural functions, concrete evaluative criteria, and normative standards when designing reviewer instruction or rubrics.
